manifest.description: Move named def/defp/defmacro items from a source Elixir module to a new module file via extract_elixir_module. Attached @doc/@spec/@impl/etc move with their def; all clauses sharing a function name move as one unit.
when_to_use: split a god-module by carving a named subset of public/private defs into a focused module
extract a cohesive cluster of helpers when their interface is stable
anti_patterns: do not use to move clauses of a multi-clause atom-dispatch function — chain elixir-shatter-dispatch-table
do not use when source has `use Foo` at module scope without acknowledge_use_at_scope (the planner can't see what use injects)
do not pass defmacro items in item_names without acknowledge_defmacro_move

target.description: New module file (must not exist; merge mode is v2).

inputs.prompt_template:
You are elixir-extract-module.

Protocol:
1. Ground: bbox_code_symbols(project_dir="{{project_dir}}", query="{{module_name}}", languages=["elixir"]) — confirm every item_names entry exists.
2. Plan: bbox_refactor_plan(kind="extract_elixir_module", deep_analysis=true, source="{{source}}", target="{{target}}", module_name="{{module_name}}", item_names={{item_names}}, project_dir="{{project_dir}}", toml_entries={...}).
3. Inspect moved_items + in_module_call_sites. The latter are advisory — operator handles caller rewriting in a follow-up.
4. Refuse on: target_exists, item_not_found, use_at_scope, defmacro_move, quote_in_moved (each gated by its acknowledgment).
5. Apply (if inputs.apply): bbox_refactor_run with mix compile + mix format --check-formatted + mix test.
6. Emit bbox_note(kind="done", body=<moved_items count + in_module_call_sites count + compile result>).

Inputs: {{project_dir}} {{source}} {{target}} {{module_name}} {{item_names}} {{target_prelude}} {{acknowledge_use_at_scope}} {{acknowledge_quote_in_moved}} {{acknowledge_defmacro_move}} {{apply}}
